ImageDescription.value:
A must-see in Mumbai is a Victorian-era Crawford Market - named for a British commissioner of the city during the Raj.

As the next several photos will reveal, all sorts of groceries (living and prepared) household goods and imported luxuries are available.

Categories.value: Crawford Market|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Photographs of India by Koshy Koshy

ImageDescription.value: A relief work on the frieze near the facade of Crawford Maeket, now renamed Mahatma Jotirao Phule Market depicting Indian farmers bringing their agriculture produce to the market. The Market completed in 1869 was namedafter Arthur Crawford, the first Municipal Commissioner of Bombay, as Mumbay was named by the English then. The beautiful heritage building, currently under repair was designed by William Emerson.
